title: Clay to Clay, and Dust to Dust
description: Clay to Clay, and Dust to Dust in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 406, “Funeral Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Clay to clay, and dust to dust! Let them min-gle, for they must! Give to earth the earth-ly clod, For the spi-rit's fled to God.

lines: Clay to clay, and dust to dust!
Let them mingle, — for they must!
Give to earth the earthly clod,
For the spirit's fled to God.
Thither let us turn our view;
Peace is there, and comfort too;
There shall those we love be found,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
